utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Usher, could you escort the witness into the courtroom and perhaps I'll meanwhile address the parties. Usually if this Chamber wants to know something from a witness, we usually ask the witness; however, the issue that was raised yesterday is one where the Chamber might not have yet at this stage of the proceedings all the information available which would make questioning of this witness on this subject effective and that's the reason why the Chamber has sought the assistance of the parties to get the information which appears to be relevant. I was informed, but please correct me if I am wrong that the conversation between the parties yesterday resulted in that you, Mr. Kehoe, will elicit the evidence from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I reread yours comments last night that you would look at the legitimate targets, that's the comment that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what of course legitimate targets -- as I said, I think I said object -- facilities, et cetera to make clear. I did not -- I choose those words in order to emphasise that I'm not seeking a long debate on what exactly is a legitimate target but about structures and about factual matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which a knowledgeable person could link with military targets, non-military targets, and whether legitimate or not, we will final be able to decide that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will read the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Leslie, my apologies for continuing another matter when you came into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that I remember still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony and as you may have noticed yesterday there are still a few matters to be covered and you will for that reason now further be examined, I would say -- I wouldn't say cross-examined, examined by Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morning, General, we would like to take off on some of the issues that was brought up by the Chamber yesterday and I would like to bring up on the screen 1D170390. I think I said -- it says on the screen -- oh, this is it, yes. General, can you just take a quick look and that and once you orient yourself I would like to ask you a few items about that. For point of reference, the UN compound is at the bottom of that picture.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you orient yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I just wanted to give you a little time to do that.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, in your first statement that has come into evidence in P84, you identified two locations as legitimate military targets. The headquarters of the north Dalmatian corps and the RSK Ministry of Defence and if we look at the designation as A1 and B1, you would agree with me the northern barracks, the Dalmatian corps is what you were talking about as A1 and the ARSK headquarters is B1, is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can go to the next slide. Now, General, in your 1996 statement you gave us additional targets which I will go through with here and for the sake of clarity, General, the plus designation next to the description are those designations that I've taken the liberty to add in this particular slide. If it doesn't have a plus designation, that means it was covered by a subsequent slide. So if you see by way of example, in the first issue the first blue box, it has northern barracks. That's the one you pointed out in your prior statement and in the prior slide. Do you understand that methodology, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now if we could just go through these particular items in your statement, you identified several items as targets and if we can move down to the B box and these would be in the bright circled areas, you have the -- you identify the parliament building which is designated as B8, you designated the Knin police station which is B10. That would be up just towards the centre of the page. Likewise, you designated a fixed the artillery position and if we're moving up to the red column here, the fixed artillery position and that is in the lower left-hand corner next to the green box which would be C3. As well as the supply depot that was next to the rail yard which is D2. Finally on these, you identified the railway station train yards, et cetera, which is designated as E8. That would be an accurate assessment of the targets that you mentioned in your statements to date; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Might I see so I can follow and make sure in my own mind that I'm answering my questions to the best of my ability. Might I be able to have a copy of my statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sure, this is a, if I may seek the assistance of the usher, Your Honour, and just for the sake of clarity, if I can read this, this is your 1 March 1996 statement, General. And I'm showing you page -- it doesn't have a page here but it's -- the number on the top is 00527690.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You can check that, General, and cross-reference it with my circles on the map to ensure that we have correctly put those in the locations that you were thinking of when you gave this statement.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Of this -- is it correct going through those particular designations as to what you were contemplating?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is. The only reason why I asked for a little bit more specificity is I can't recall if that's the exact location of C3, the rebel Serb anti-aircraft facility, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Now, let us move to the next item and General, I will tell you that this is series of items that we go through a question about. It is not in your witness statement so just so you're not looking through it. These are just some other issues. Again, as we go through this going through the next slide, you'll see the plus marks next to various designations and those are the items that we're going to go through. I think we are -- yeah. Is that the next one? Yeah, it is, okay. I apologise, I got ahead of myself. Yes, it is. Now, let us just go through. Now, A2 in the centre of this slide. A2 has a circle around it. That was the barracks known as the Senjak barracks for the ARSK, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Were those the facilities where the families of the officers lived?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It was a military barracks in -- run by the ARSK in, as you can see, towards the centre of town. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but in that location, I believe that was -- I stand to be corrected and I apologise if I'm wrong, I believe those were the families residence of the ARSK officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us move to A3. Now, that is down here you which is a another ARSK facility that was next to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And now up to A4, the high school, do you see that at the top?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, there was an ARSK unit garrisoned at that high school, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I spent five months living in Knin. I'm not aware of any military activity taking place in that school and with the utmost respect, I'd like to see such evidence before I either agree or disagree with your contention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Leslie, to judge upon the evidence which would be presented would not -- we are just asking you whether you know. Apparently, you do not know. But whether -- I can imagine in your profession, you sometimes ask you to bring you the information and to give a judgement on the matter but here, we are interested in what you know and not, at this moment, in any judgement on the basis of evidence presented to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did you talk to Mr. Dreyer during the course of the day on the 4th when he was going out to pick up UN personnel; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, no, I don't recall. I'm sure I did, but I can't recall any specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did he tell you that the ARSK had a mortar in placement up by the high school on the 4th?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall that conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we go down to A5, the location for the ARSK special police. If I may, before we go to that, sir, in the high school, you're familiar with the concept of dual use, are you not, for a target?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And correct me if I am wrong, but when you look at a building or target that would normally be -- can be civilian and can be military in order to make a decision, on for instance this high school, you have to know what it's used for at the time such as a mortar in placement?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go down to A 5 which is the special police. Are you familiar with that location as the location of the special police?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see on the map, there was a police office in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the police in the former Yugoslavia often times had combat functions as well, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go to the next page. I do believe I've covered everything in that, which is the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, in order to avoid whatever confusion where I just said that we would like to know from the witness what he remembers, what his memory tells him, of course this does not prevent you from refreshing memory which is something different from giving evidence and then asking for a judgement, but of course refreshment of memory is of course admissible as it always is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, this is, as you can see, the plus marks are down in the B column, under command and control. B2 is known as the old hospital. Do you recall that there was a part of the Ministry of Defence at that location?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: B3 known as the senior's hotel. Do you know that was used as a ARSK officers' accommodation?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not. I beg your pardon. I am aware that officers and their families lived in a facility which approximates that of the circle on the map so in part I knew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that would reflect B3?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officers and their families, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You previously said that officers and their families were in A2?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were quite a lot of accommodations that were used for officers and their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And B4, do you recall that was the residence of President Martic?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the B5 over to the right-hand side, did you recall that was the republic of Serb -- the headquarters of the republic of Serb Krajina State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that was also a depot or another rail yard there too, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a rail junction there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, B6, again, moving downtown, do you recall that that was their communications centre?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And B7, their telegraph and post centre, right along the middle of the road downtown?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, that was the location of the post office, yes. So in part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the -- number 8, B8 which is part of the parliament complex, that also included RSK television. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And B9, if I may, B9 over to the right -- actually, just right of centre, that would have been the power distribution centre, would it not? If you recall.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sorry, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, I think Chamber just wants you to say what you recall. Now, we move to the next map which is designated ARSK anti-aircraft unit. General, I have attempted to put -- and we're going to talk about the items that are on the red block to the right and you can see them circled in bold starting with C1. The anti-aircraft artillery headquarters; do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: C2, another anti-artillery -- excuse me, anti-aircraft artillery position; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall some anti-aircraft systems being in that rough area. I will certainly accept the precision with which you've drawn it on the map, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe we've discussed C3 towards the bottom and now C4.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I don't see C4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Actually it is, it should be down towards the bottom -- excuse me, there it is. I knew I saw it last night. An anti-aircraft position that was virtually behind your Sector South headquarters; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely and that was a very large anti-aircraft facility which covered some ground, very complexed and lots of weapons systems in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can move to the next chart. The box that we will be discussing is the pink-purplish box described RSK military industries and depots. The D1 in the centre of the page, the Tvik factory, do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: D3, the Kninjanka factory and depot, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And up in the bluff should be D4, and that is right along the Krka river, if you may, do you see that large area that's circled to the left. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And there were a series of various military depots stretched along that area that has been circled as D4; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe we've covered that. Now, let us move to the next chart: Transportation and movement infrastructure. I think this is, frankly, General, this is going to take a little patience to get through because the numbers are a little bit all over the place. They are attempted to be sequentially on the box but if we take our time going through this, I think we can get through it. From the railway lines, we talk about E1 and that was a railroad tunnel.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, may I -- are you asking me if I remember these or are you asking me if I'm aware that they were used by the military?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm asking if you are aware of them.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Yes, I am aware of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that would have been a tunnel. Do you recall a tunnel in that location?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I never physically saw a tunnel, but we were aware that there was a tunnel system which exited in that approximate region.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: E2, now of course -- let's just take this, if we go to E1, there was a track in E3 and then a tunnel going down into E2; is that basically your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't actually recall but I'm aware that there was a tunnel system in that region.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Staying with this, sir, there was track system -- if we look at E4 just a little bit further, there were tracks, trail road tracks there and yet further up in E5 as well?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the best of my recollection, those were tracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And likewise if we go to the bottom of the page, we see E6?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: More tracks. And E7 would have been, and that's next -- by E2 towards the centre of the page, there was a road and railway overpass there, wasn't there? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, E8 is the item that you discussed previously which is the main railway station. And E9 -- excuse me, right next to E6 there was a -- do you recall there being a railway maintenance area in that location?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And E10, do you recall there being a railway bridge at that location?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And E11, likewise a railway bridge?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was also used by non- -- it was used by things other than trains but got it, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, E12 was the ARSK helipad; do you recall them turning a soccer field into a helipad?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall the ARSK turning the soccer field into a helipad though I'm aware that helicopters would he occasionally land either there or in what you have circled as E8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Moving into the E13 area, that was the main crossroad or junction, the roundabout in the centre of Knin; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that was the transit -- do you recall that as a transit road in various directions going in and out of Knin?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, just for my understanding in the early stages of your testimony, I think you referred -- I think two times to roundabout or at least -- was it that location that you referred to at that time? I would have to find your exact words, but I remember that you did it twice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: E14, sir, that is the bridge, I guess, relatively close to the UN barracks, there was, in fact, a bridge at that location?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the last one that we have on this item is E15 and that was, of course, another overpass. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I'm not disputing that there might well be an overpass there. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And again, General, this is just your recollection, I understand. Just go to the next chart putting together the items that we've looked at. Other than the items that we've said that you didn't recall, would this basically correspond to the areas that you just pointed out in these various charts that we discussed?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I have no further questions of this witness on this score and I would like to move this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This series of pictures, and they are uploaded as a series, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think so. I'd like an opportunity to look at the captions if that's possible but in principle, no, but I just haven't had a chance to study them in any detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, Mr. Tieger I take it that you can do that before Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Oh, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Even if later today you could verify whether this overall picture reflects because that's apparently your concern what we saw on the earlier ones to verify whether this is an accurate total of what we've seen before, if you could give us that today then we could immediately deal with this exhibit. Mr. Registrar, it would be marked for identification for the time being.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D131 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Tieger, would you have any questions in addition to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General Leslie, I'd like to craft my follow-up questions in a manner which doesn't necessarily take us through each of the documents that you just reviewed although we may be returning to those. First of all, let me ask you, looking at the last document that we saw, the last page of the exhibit. Did you observe corrected fire on August 4th or August 5th that was located in areas not covered in -- or not blocked out in red?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And can you point out where those would be?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I have the centre block expanded? Sir, I'm not quite sure of the appropriateness of my question, but when you say within the blocks in red, for example, the block that covers the train yard, the train track itself is about two metres wide. This block of ground is about 6 to 700 metres wide. Do I include targets inside that block or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, you're correct that the manner in which I asked the question would have precluded that but I appreciate the clarification and I'm sure the Court does as well. So if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not bound by the exact way in which Mr. Kehoe shaped the area. I mean if you'd say, I consider the railway facilities to be not exactly the shape that was given on this map, then you're free to explain that and to include any targeting in your answer which, in your view, would not be covered by the description you gave earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Because most of the targets, of course, are pinpoint, and these blocks of ground are red are not. So may have this centre block expanded even more, please. Okay. Might I suggest the colour of my instrument?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These colours were -- has meaning, blue is any marking made on request of the Defence and I take it that you have now a different colour in your -- if it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If there's any trouble viewing it, I'm sure the Court will -- we can fix that in some manner but as the Judge mentioned, there is he's a protocol here for the colours used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Might I suggest we just move back to P62 which is the map and that might be easier still.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think for purposes of this question, this is probably more ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A bit against the protocol, the usher has changed the colours slightly so as not to have it exactly the same red as we find it on this map. If we can't see it, we'll find another way of resolving this problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, these are indicative of areas. My memory is not sufficiently robust to be able to give you a precise location of where I saw what I believed to be adjusted fire. Sir, that to the best of my recollection, they are the general blocks where I saw what I believed to be adjusted fire which do not necessarily correspond with the areas that were outlined by Defence counsel. A word of explanation on the estimated, the visibility -- I'm sorry, I'll stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, when you say adjusted fire or corrected fire, does that mean corrected fire into the residential neighbourhood in contrast to the process of correcting fire --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I object to the leading. If they're asking a particular question then obviously --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course the question could be: If it was adjusted was it adjusted in the direction of what is depicted here as a potential military target or was it not in that direction. That's -- I take it that's more neutrally formulated. But I think it's clear what Mr. Tieger and what the Chamber would like to know whether the adjustment could be explained by you on the basis of your experience as moving towards any of the red dots indicated here or any of the red areas or whether you could not observe that it was done in that direction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, there were some instances when the fire that I saw, which I believe to be adjusting or in the adjustment process was not fire which would logically indicate that the fire was being shifted towards those areas indicated by Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have still one puzzle. You added some something in writing on the top and your handwriting appears to be as bad as mine. Could you explain to me what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, "estimated" and the reason why I cannot be more precise is there were two main vantage points from Sector South headquarters, one of which was the balcony opposite my office and that of my commander's office. The second is from the region of the helipad which has got a greater elevation and the roof line that you can see from both those locations obviously differed according to altitude. From the helipad region, you could see the explosions breaking the roof line in this region and a ball of greasy grey smoke, a plume of debris would break the roof line, but it is difficult to be precise as to where the round landed with any degree of certainty within a couple of hundred metres. So I don't want to mislead the Court in trying to portray that I know more information than I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, in conjunction with that comment, I don't know it came across in the transcript, but the General put a square -- added a square to that area as he was discussing, if I am going to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, he added the square to that. One very technical question, Mr. Registrar, does the upper part where some markings are, will that be included in the exhibit as it will be finally stored? Yes. So it's the whole of the picture. Even if it goes beyond the -- what seems to be an aerial photograph. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, let me ask this question in order to determine the extent to which we need to go through individual identified locations that were depicted on the exhibit shown to you. First of all, there were a number of locations that you were shown about which you indicated you were unfamiliar. With respect to those locations with which you were familiar, did all of those, to the best of your recollection, were all of those used by the military immediately prior to August 4th and did they in furtherance of the RSK military effort and if not, perhaps we should go through those and see which of them you were aware were being used by the military and if so in what manner.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not aware or I -- I'm not aware of the usage of the facilities outlined by Defence vis-a-vis the contention that they were used for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Your Honour I may return to that after some additional questions and I also wanted the Court to be aware of that because the Court may wish to return, but I'm going to continue first and then perhaps return to the individual sites.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the previous answer is not entirely clear to me. You said, "I'm not aware of the usage of the facilities outlined by Defence vis-a-vis the contention that they were used for military purposes." Now, we have a variety of facilities or -- for example, a railway complex, if you've got a train even at a distance of 25 kilometres from there, of course there is some potential of that facility to be used for military purposes. Of course, if you're talking about barracks, well, they are used or they are not used or they are used in a certain way as you hinted at earlier, perhaps for accommodating staff and/or their families. So your answer is not entirely clear. Where you say that there was a, apparently, artillery battery, then when you described that, it gave me at least the impression that it was an active battery so therefore, that would be something that would be active to say so. Could you try to give us a bit of a better impression than you gave in your previous answer on what you actually are not, perhaps, for everything in detail because you don't have to go to every part of the railway track and this Chamber understands that if you demolish a railway track here, that there might not be a great military need to demolish it at a distance of 100 metres again unless there is any side track or something like that. So could you give us, perhaps without going into detail for all of that, perhaps using categories saying -- to tell us what -- what your awareness was as active military use of those facilities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The -- what I call the headquarters north Dalmatian corps which, if you could -- would you like me to pinpoint these sites, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just wondering how much we get on this picture if we go on. Perhaps if we would go back. If we store this one and have another one to mark what you are telling us now. Mr. Registrar, this one would then be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit P85 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P85. Is there any objection against P85?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P85 is admitted into evidence. And then let's then go back to the document as it was. And could you please -- we can't change zooming in and zooming out anymore once you started marking. Is this the picture you would like to have or would you like to have it wider or more narrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, if I might suggest if we go back to what Defence put on the screen vis-a-vis the seven categories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Categories.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which I outlined in my statement of the 1st of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that would be the last -- no not necessarily the last --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's the second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The second --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Slide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The second slide in the series.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That, Your Honours, for the sake of clarity is the combination General of both the targets that you mentioned in the 12 April [sic] 1995 statement and the targets that are before you in the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Here we have the categories. If you could perhaps deal with them by category.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just one correction, Judge, I noted in my comment that I said 12 April 1995, that's 12 August 1995. My apologies, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we first then concentrate on troop bases and barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. With the addition of the special police headquarters in this region here, those are the only facilities of which I'm aware being used on or about the period immediately prior to the 4th of August for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A few slides further down, we get a more complete picture of all the facilities in the different categories. Could we perhaps move on to, I think, three or four slides further.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may assist the Court, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you looking at the -- we followed them in this progression.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but of course we're now looking back at the totality. So if we would have the one with most of the details so that we can -- if we're talking about two bases and barracks that we have all the troops bases and barracks mentioned so that we know what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe that would be -- all the bases and barracks, I believe, is in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but for all of the categories.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That would be the sheet that I think we had just talked about. If we can just go through them and glance at them quickly and, Your Honour, I can pick out the ones that you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was the -- I think the semi last one because the last one didn't give any text anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. It is the one that's on the transport infrastructure, it should be page 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 7, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It notes at the top transport and movement infrastructure. I believe that's the one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the one that gives -- although it does not highlight everything, but mainly the transport infrastructure, it gives at least a listing of all the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It does highlight them, Your Honour. However, I -- we broke them into categories simply so we could designate them and highlight them and it would be easier for points of reference. That being said, I do believe that all of these circles in all of these charts are set forth in this diagram. However, the ones that were not being discussed under transport and infrastructure just have a lighter colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes that's the difference between lighting and highlighting. Please proceed. Mr. Leslie, could you on the basis of these categories and having now available to yourself also the detailed information further tell us what you know about these facilities being active for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, A11 [sic], which was the headquarters of the north Dalmatian corps was a barracks which obviously acted as the node for the rebel Serb fighting organisation that was located in this part of the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, I don't mean to interrupt, I believe the General is talking about A1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I had some difficulties in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, A1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In terms of the air Defence battery C4, that was a large complex well fortified air defence command and control centre with active radars and missiles occupied by several hundred Serbian soldiers -- sorry, ARSK soldiers and its use was exclusive military. The train yards which are indicated as a very large circle E8, of course that is an area -- a large area, very large area indicated on the map and of course train yards, train tracks and train yards themselves are relatively pin point, so at what point does one wish to attack and disrupt the train yards, it would not cover such area but as you mentioned, sir, it does have potential to use. The ministry of Defence is the ministry of defence complex which is in the area of B1. That also includes what I call the ARSK headquarters which is offset from the road and tucked in behind the Ministry of Defence. That was in use as a command and control node as offices and as -- well, the traditional functions of a nation's Ministry of Defence. The government house to which Defence referred, that was in use by the leaders of the Krajina. The supply depot, which is in the area of D2 and there was some military activity in that region. I never actually got inside the gate, so I can't tell you what sort of activity but there were soldiers in and around that facility, certainly on the last time I saw which is roughly the 2nd or the 3rd. The police headquarters which is at B10 was the centre for the Knin localised police force which as Defence quite properly pointed out in my opinion the police forces had a quasi role, both military and civil. I also agree with Defence in that A5, the special police headquarters was located in that region, if memory serves, and they likewise had a quasi military role. And though it's not in Knin so not necessarily part of my original testimony, the air defence facilities at C1, C2 -- I mean we were aware there was something up there and I'm not certainly not quibbling about the precise indication on the map. As well, the bunker facilities in the region of D4, such bunker facilities existed though, of course, they're outside the municipal bounds or the built-up area of Knin. Those are, to the best of my recollection, sir, the military facilities of which I'm aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For example, the Tvik factory D1, did you have any awareness of active military use of those -- of that facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I -- no, I do not. I cannot say what they were used for. I never got inside, even though I would at times walk right by that facility, I never got inside the compound. I hadn't -- it was -- there were in that region, I would see occasionally on my walks to work Serb males wearing fatigues, usually the bottom half of the fatigues with a sort of a heavier jackets on top who would be occasionally coming and going into that facility, but I never saw military equipments inside there, either being delivered or exiting. That's the extent of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, with respect to the locations you've indicated had -- were either being used in some manner by the military or had some potential military value, did you have an opportunity to see either before you left Knin to take up your position in Zagreb or after you took up your position in Zagreb the damage done to those facilities during the course of the shelling on August 4th and August 5th?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And were you able to observe whether or not the damage to those facilities was consistent with a -- with the fire intended to destroy or neutralise each of those targets. That is, was it you see fire consistent with corrected fire on to those targets.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you rephrase the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure. You indicated that you had an chance to see what kind of damage was done to those facilities?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did that indicate to you based on your experience and back ground whether or not those particular targets had been the subject of an effort concerted effort to destroy or neutralise them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think we're in an area of what did he see and I just object to that score and ask if we stay in this particular location as to what he observed at these targets when he had the opportunity to go back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course I'm aware that asking for consistency in a certain context is always a mixed issue, some facts, some assessment. Let me ask you the following: When you looked at the damage, did it ever come to your mind, did you say, on the basis of the damage I see, it comes to my mind that this facility was targeted, on the basis of your observation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I would say the air defence battery located at C4 was deliberately targeted and well and truly covered by Croatian army indirect fire assets. It was effectively neutralised. And so there was deliberate attempts to adjust the fire on to that battery, which were successful and that put an end to that facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you will not be surprised that of course what interests us most is those facilities which are near to residential areas, whether, there, on the basis of your observation, it ever came to your mind, did you say, Well, the damage is the same for all of the town or here, you see a type of damage which brought into your mind that this was specifically targeted, at least on the basis of the damage it looked as if it was specifically targeted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, throughout the shelling, we could not figure out, as military professionals, what the Croatian army were shooting at. We understood them shooting at the battery. We did not understand the targeting criteria they were using to distribute fire across the rest of the town, and I saw very little evidence of the military targets that I outlined with the exception of the air defence battery actually being hit in significant manner, neutralised or destroyed. So it was confusing and puzzling to us what the Croatians were actually shooting at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask a question that was the subject of some discussion yesterday that I think the -- we couldn't reach accord on with the Defence so they know in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean is it dealing with this targeting issue because I don't know if we had any other discussions to have an accord on. I think the accord that was going to come as to who was going to begin the questioning this morning and we elected to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if it doesn't ring a bell to you then we'll see whether that is still the case after Mr. Tieger has put his question to the witness. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The discussion was with Mr. Misetic. I believe he knows what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General Leslie, you've had an opportunity to see some of the -- well, to see the alleged military targets identified on the exhibit, some of which you indicated in an earlier response to the Court were pinpoint and some of which looked broader. And I want to ask you a question that I tried to ask the other day. And that is whether the indirect weapons systems, the rockets and howitzers were able to distinguish between the pinpoint targets and the civilian structures around them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you answer that question, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, this is what we objected to before with regard to this weapons system and if we go back through this, I would ask the Court for recross on this score. On the first point this was part of the direct examination where the witness offered a particular opinion but if we're going to go into area targeting then I would ask to open up a recross and we'll get into an actual area targeting history and the geometry of it. My understanding for this morning's issue was an identification of the Court as to what possible targets were in and around the Knin area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, for your question to have a proper factual basis, at least we would have to know what the knowledge of this witness is exactly about the weapons that were available, the weapons that were used and what weapons used -- what weapons caused what kind of damage. Another matter, of course, is what is the position of those weapons, the position of those weapons isn't that true that that is usually described in all kinds of documentary -- a lot of testing has been done. Is there any need at this moment to go into any further detail. We know distances.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason -- I think we addressed a number of if not all of the issues the Court just raised earlier in the witness 's testimony. I had asked this very question of the witness. The Court indicated, as I recall, that it was in the context, at that time, to theoretical or abstract because there might be, for example, structures, military targets that were of great size. It wasn't linked to the particular targets or particular locations and I deferred for that reason. Now that the witness has been presented with the alleged military targets in the context of ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me try to understand what I'd like to know and ask Mr. Leslie. Mr. Leslie, in view of the knowledge you have, and please explain what your knowledge was of the weaponry used, is it your experience or what would you find in your domestic instructions as to whether those weapons would have such a position that they could be used for the targets we find on this map -- the facilities that we find on this map. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, as a soldier, there are two broad categories of targets when it comes to size. One is pinpoint, and one is an area. Pinpoint can be just as the name implies, relatively small, tens, thirties in metres an area can be anywhere from 200 to 400 metres or even larger. The area targets of A1, C4, and E8 were just that. Most other targets were pinpoint. The technology available to the Croatian army at that time of which I have absolute confidence and certainty in my statement was not capable of engaging pinpointing targets without a significant risk of collateral damage and they would be extraordinarily fortunate to achieve a first round hit at any range from any angle, at any elevation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What does your military handbook tell you if, as alternatives, for using the type of weaponry that apparently was used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, if you do not have a certain degree of precision and a certain guarantee, though there are no absolutes in war, that you can engage a military facility or a facility which is being used for military purposes in an area which is full of civilian structures and people, then you do not engage it using area or indiscriminate weapons systems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Mr. Tieger, any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With regard to the weapons systems that you're talking about, in order to give an assessment of those weapons systems, General, you need to know the range of that weapon; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, would you say that it is -- indirect fire weapons system is more accurate at 1.000 metres than -- excuse me, at say 5 kilometres as opposed to 10?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not always the case, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, can it be the case?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And so in order to assess whether or not something has been firing accurately, you would have to know the range, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in order to know the margin of error of an indirect fire system, you have to know what was the actual weapon, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you don't know what weapons were fired on individual locations, do you?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if we go through this, sir, if I may. As we go through and we enter into a particular area, is it your testimony that under no circumstances is an area in and around Knin an area that can be hit with indirect fire?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me go back to -- it's 1D170398.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm going to put another document on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, I put this document and I have reimposed the red circles that we talked about previously as well as the green areas being unpopulated areas. If we should go to the next chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should we give the witness at least a moment to look at it because it's not very clear to me and I don't know whether he could confirm or contest the -- what are populated and what are not populated areas on the whole of this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, there are some areas which are circled in red which I believe had displaced persons in them in the period immediately prior to the 4th of August. Most of the areas that you've circled in green, though, were not heavily populated by civil personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can move to the next chart. Now, we're just focussing on this particular location being in the general downtown area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Have you got that located, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the yellow circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next chart. Now, I've given the dimensions of this particular locale and if we can blow that up. I believe during the course of your testimony previously, you gave us a margin of error on one location of 600 metres by 420 metres, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I may have those numbers incorrect. Sir, look at this particular location. In this particular location, we have a -- from north to south -- excuse me, from the top to the bottom, 360 metres and at one point across, it is 1180 metres. Now, that is an area that includes multiple circles that we talked about this morning, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You referred to those circles, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in those circles, sir, that is an area where an indirect fire system can be used; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in every location. Not in my opinion in every location, because there were civilian structures and facilities within the probable error of range no matter what the direction of fire was from no matter what type of Croatian artillery system was employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So let me just take you off on that with an issue that Judge Orie just asked you with regard to alternatives. Now, number one, sir, you know that the -- a military is or combatant is prohibited from putting military targets in civilian areas; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So is it your testimony, General, that you do not believe that it is prohibited for a combatant to put a military facility in a civilian area?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, my intent -- my reply is not meant to sound disrespectful or flippant, but Canada's ministry of national defence is located in downtown Ottawa, that is not an illegal act.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, does putting a military facility in a civilian area make that target immune from attack?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- no, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you are aware that during NATO strikes in Kosovo, that significant collateral damage took place in the bombing campaign because the Serbs put military facilities in civilian areas; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take your contention for it, I was not personally involved in the NATO air strikes in Kosovo, I wasn't on the ground, so yes, I -- I take your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when does collateral damage as a result of the Serbs putting those locations in military facilities in civilian locations, when the bombing of those locations caused collateral damage to civilian structures and personnel, there was no NATO person ever charged with any type of indiscriminate attack --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, whether someone is charged or not is an interesting issue but not something to be put to the witness with a clear suggestion that if you are not charged, that you didn't commit a crime which I take it from your professional experience you would not confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The average student that's 16 years of age in the Netherlands has committed 13.7 crimes, not all of them very serious, and was not charged for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's an amazing statistic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's 30 years old, it might have improved or degenerated since then. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But when attacks takes place on military targets placed in civilian areas, the NATO experience is that collateral damage takes place, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not always. Rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well if in fact there is a mistake or collateral damage, that does not thereby mean that the actual firing on that location was improper, does it?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Does it necessarily?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If there's a mistake involved or there is a collateral damage on firing on a military target, are you saying that per se, there is fault involved?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two types of mistakes in such categories. The first is the choice of weapons system which, if it has an inherent indiscriminate attributes which can't be directed precisely to a pinpoint target then it is a mistake of the point of origin of fire. The second mistake is in the target analysis in terms of attributing certain military or civilian attributes to specific structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry go ahead?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third type of mistake which can occur is a natural human error either in the point of origin of the fire or from the observer who is correcting the target grid procedure. Those are the three broad categories of mistake in all professional armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in looking at these -- I'm sorry. When looking at these particular targets and when NATO looks at a particular target, they look at whether or not it is not of -- excuse me, let me rephrase that. NATO makes the determination of this target not whether or not it is of military use but one of it could be of military use, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not always.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please make pauses, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They do on occasion, don't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The potential military use of targets is part of any decision cycle within most NATO nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And as part of that particular decision cycle, NATO has made a decision that often times strategic targets are items that should be targeted even though they are not immediately involved in the military usage; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't think of one at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to the attack on Serbia. How about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, let's -- I let you go for a while and I do not mind if you think it's of great importance to analyse what happened in attacks by other armed forces elsewhere in the world, but I'd very much like to focus on this case. One of the problems is that if you're talking about attacks by the armed forces of country X against a city in country Y, that would first have to receive all the information relevant for that and then we could only further make sensible use of this information, but not in general terms. Some of the questions, of course, whether if collateral damage occurs, whether that's always wrong, I think that we have sufficient case law already alone in this Tribunal that collateral damage should be avoided by the weaponry you choose, et cetera, et cetera, but these kind of sweeping statements, and that's of course the problems with your questions at this moment is that they are of a very nature, whereas usually decisions to be taken depend on five, six, seven, ten, fifteen relevant aspects of the situation we're dealing with. Therefore, again, the monocausal sweeping statement approach does not always assist the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do understand that, Judge. I was responding to the rather sweeping statements presented by the Office of the Prosecutor by not asking concerning particular targets being hit in these areas designated by the General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They at least stayed within the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let me just go back to this and I will move on off the strategic targets issue. It is not your position, is it, that by the RSK putting, for instance, their military headquarters in a civilian area, you're not saying that that makes the facility immune from shelling, does it?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not make it immune from shelling if the shelling system had a certain degree of guarantee as to precision to minimise collateral damage, otherwise, sir, if there is a high-risk of significant collateral damage or of not hitting the target with the first couple of rounds, yes, it has -- enjoys a certain degree of immunity considering the risk of collateral damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So your position with regard to and moving back into the Krajina, your position with regard to the RSK headquarters and place yourself in August 4, 1995 is your position by putting the RSK headquarters in a civilian area it rendered it immune from shelling; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you -- when you -- I'm sorry, I just need a bit more precision. When you say shelling, are you talking about the shelling systems of the time or are you talking about the shelling systems of today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, in order to avoid whatever confusion earlier, page 35 line 4, your question was about immunity from attack. We now have a new series of questions which talks about immunity from shelling and, I think, Mr. Leslie rightfully seeks to know exactly what your question is about. That is where he, Mr. Leslie, earlier referred to the technological aspects. We should be very precise on what you are asking him. Immunity, it appears from the answers, that it depends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And Judge I -- in looking at the question and my apologies, General. My question was not precise enough in the sense that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the sense that, General, I was talking about the weapons systems in 1995, I'm not talking about sophisticated weaponry that may be available in 2008, so I stand corrected and I apologise. So let me go back and re-ask that question. So is it your position giving the weapons systems that were available in August of 1995, did the placing by the RSK of their Ministry of Defence in a civil -- an area populated by civilians, did that immunise that facility from being shelled?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, you -- and let me go back to one of your documents and I forget what the P document was. Mr. Monkhouse, it was the one with the square. Yes, the one that he drew. I believe it's P85, I have been told by Ms. Katalinic.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, would you like me to try to expand on my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are a variety of factors which any commander must go through before deciding which weapons systems must be used to engage what type of target. So the decision of the RSK to have their Ministry of Defence where it was surrounded by civilian structures has not rendered it immune. Immune is a very strong term, it's an absolute, and I can think of circumstances wherein it would be more than, it would be quite legitimate to engage the RSK Ministry of Defence with imprecise indirect fire systems and that only -- that circumstance if there were no civilians in the potential beaten zone of the weapons that were being used to engage that target. So hopefully that clarifies my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So General, to -- taking this to its logical conclusion, in 1995, the best way to secure your military facilities and render them virtually immune from the shelling systems available to the HV at the time was to place them in civilian areas; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I mean the witness has been asked this question twice. I didn't -- although I had some concerns about the use of the term "immune" which has connotations that may not be precisely relevant to the inquiry here, I didn't object. But now the witness has already answered this question twice, explained it, and now this is -- we're moving into the area of argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from that, Mr. Kehoe, you're asking for logical conclusions from what we heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Once again, Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please rely on abilities to draw logical conclusions on what we heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I fall back on as Mr. Cayley always does, the fault of our upbringing so I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether Mr. Cayley is guilty or not is still to be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He's always guilty, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Leslie, you -- when you drew this square in, I believe, it's P85, you were in the compound, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. And sir, this square is not meant to be totally restrictive. I mean there were other regions but it -- I'd have to think about it deeply to give you more precise locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe. I don't know whether we are talking about the same square, but it's my recollection that Mr. Leslie was in this courtroom when he drew this square. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Once again it's imprecision when he observed the locations of the impact in this square.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that's what you asked him if that's what Mr. Leslie understood your question to be, then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General I think you understood what I was talking about as imprecise as my question was. You were drawing a square and you were commenting on impacts in a particular area while you were observing them from the UN compound; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And sir as you look at this, you have no idea what -- where these shells actually landed, do you?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have an idea in terms of we could see the dust cloud and the ball breaking the roofline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm stopping you Mr. Leslie. Mr. Kehoe, has this not been talked about by the witness, the roof line, et cetera, et cetera, several times and what he has seen from the helicopter position, what he saw from the balcony. Unless there's anything new what you specifically want to know about, that's my recollection of what the witness told us two times at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would finish just covering that he had no why idea the point of impact and no idea of the point of origin and the only thing he saw was the smoke. Your Honour, it needs no further clarification on that. I will simply tender P57 into evidence, and I will complete my examination. Excuse me, did I tender it? Actually, it's not P57 it's 1D170398 the chart that we talked about before going to 1D170400.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To be quite honest, I'm lost whether this was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's the one that we were talking about previously with the geometric lines going across that I had not tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that one I think. Mr. Tieger any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Only that I -- well, if I could reserve that, Your Honour, I recall there was some suggestion that it was -- may have been grounded on incorrect information and in terms of specificity, again in principle, no objection but I do want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'd like to hear from you not later than by Monday. Mr. Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D132 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Tieger, we have no fixed rules for examination of witnesses on specific request of the Chamber. As I said before, usually the Chamber would put questions to the witness itself. We might have a few questions even for you after the break so therefore, we will have a break for 25 minutes. We will resume at 11.00 and then we hope that we'll be able to release you soon after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Leslie, Judge Kinis would have a few questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Mr. Leslie, could you please clarify the hierarchy of the relationship between organisations which are operated based on your mandate at that time in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the terms of the United Nations, United Nations protection force headquarters in Zagreb was the superior headquarters to UNCRO, also located in Zagreb which was the superior headquarters to United Nations Sector South. In Sector South, there was detachments of UN civil servants, United Nations military observers and United Nations civilian police. Were you asking me about the United Nations structure, sir, or the local Serb? I may have misunderstood?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Local -- in Knin directly.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, sir. You had the Republika Srpska. Subordinate to that, you had the ARSK which was the fighting arm of the Republika Srpska. You also had special police which were much more paramilitary than the normal police. You had the normal police who were themselves paramilitary in the sense that they did military activities and functions to a limited extent. There were elements of the Bosnian Serb army that I believe were active in some measure in and amongst the ARSK elements. Sir, does that answer your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Not directly. Maybe I'm not correctly asking you this question. My question was there were UNMO, CIVPOL and HRAT and this chain of hierarchy, how was, in your organisation directly and were their headquarters were located at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within Sector South we had the normal Sector South troops there was also an UNMO detachment which was supporting General Forand but their chain of command went from the Sector South detachment directly to the UNMO headquarters which was in Zagreb. There were detachments of UNMOs which were down in the same terrain allocations of the line battalions in the zone of separation, and they worked with them, but they did not work for them. So they were independent. In terms of UNCIVPOL, the exact same command and control architecture was replicated so at Sector South headquarters, we had an UNCIVPOL detachment which worked with us but not for us, and the UNCIVPOL headquarters in turn in Zagreb would provide the command and control architecture and guidance to the UNCIVPOL elements throughout UNCRO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: You mentioned in your statement that blockade of compound start on the 5th of August. How long did it last and how it affects the work of all these organisations?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the blockade essentially went into effect sometime around 11.30, 1100 hours on the 5th of August and I'm sorry I can't be more precise on the times without referring to my notes. And it was certainly in effect when I left Sector South and Knin on the 7th. There were -- in terms of its effect, essentially it meant that none of those organisations could leave the compound so in terms of what they actually did outside work ground to a standstill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would also have a few questions for you. First question: Did you ever have any personal dealings with one of the accused in this case, that is Mr. Gotovina, Mr. Cermak or Mr. Markac?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had personal dealings, sir, with both Generals Gotovina and Cermak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I can't be precise on the dates, but I met General Gotovina for the first time when I accompanied General Kutil the former sector commander whom General Forand replaced sometime in the end of March/early April time frame and there were or three or four, perhaps four other occasions when I was accompanying either General Kutil or General Forand when he had discussions with General Gotovina. With regards to General Cermak I first met General Cermak when he arrived at Sector South headquarters on or about the 6th of August to indicate that he was assuming the post of the -- essentially the military governor of the region and I subsequently had meetings with him, three, fourish over the subsequent three months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's when you had moved already to Zagreb, so you met him only once when you were still in Knin, is that ...

utterances.speaker: ANDREW LESLIE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, as far as your meetings with General Gotovina, as you said was concerned, that was -- could you tell us whether any of the conversations you had at that time you considered to be of direct relevance for what happened on the 4th and the 5th of August and the days after that? If you tell us what the subject of the conversations were, approximately.
