utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections from either Defence counsel. Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P89, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P89 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Ms. Frolich.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we show 65 ter number 04846.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Mr. Sovilj, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: This document is, as far as I can see, just one part of the list of people missing or killed in Operation Storm who hailed from the territory of Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Is there any information on this -- in this document that is familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: I would just like to say that there's some family names that hail from the territory of Knin, not only from Gracac. I'm familiar with the name of my father, Vlade Sovilj, father's name, Mile; and then Danica Sovilj, whose father's name was Milos. I'm also familiar with the name of Nebojsa, Surle; Ilija, Orla and Nedeljeko Petar.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you just read the numbers that are next to the these names that you recognise of your father and Danica Sovilj.

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: 22 in front of my father, and 23 in front of Danica Sovilj.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Could you read please the date of your father?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: 27 November 1931.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: And the number that's in the column --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Frolich.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you want to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Chamber is I would say perfectly able to read 22, 23, 25 and the 1931 instead of 1930 as the date of birth of the father of this witness. You want to tender this document into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P90, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. P90 is admitted into evidence if you have any further questions which go beyond just reading what the document says, please proceed, Ms. Frolich.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: No, thank you, I'm done with this document. Now could 65 ter 03820 be shown on screen and at the same time, would it be possible to show the hard copy of the exhibit as well to the witness, namely just some portions that are translated are part of the same document unless it is easy to go to a different page in the same document at the same time. That would be page 1 in English and page 22 is the portion that's -- the same portion that's translated into B/C/S. That's also number X0164071. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Mr. Sovilj, on the screen in front of you -- have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: Indeed, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: When did you see this document for the first time?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: Yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Is there any information in this document on this page that is familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: Well, a reference is made here to the cigarette box and the word used here is tobajara that's the word used for the object in case.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Thank you. Could this document be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We hear of no objections.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P91, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P91 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Thank you. Can 65 ter 04845 be shown. Could we zoom in a little bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photo?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Where did you see this photo?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: Here, yesterday, in your office.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: What do you -- is there anything on this photo that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: Again, I can see the same metal tobacco case, but I'm also familiar with the pull over -- I believe that my father had a very similar if not an identical pull over.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Can you go to the next page of this 65 ter? Do you recognise this photo and what is on this photo?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: Yes. The metal cigarette case appears again, the tobajara.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: If both photographs in this 65 ter number could be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P92, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that's the series of photographs, P92 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Mr. Sovilj, is this tobacco case, is this the same tobacco case that you talk about earlier as belonging to your father?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: As far as I can see, I believe so, as far as I can tell.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 14 of your statement, you talk about your native village of Kijani being hit. Can you briefly explain what you meant by that? To be clear, this is page 3 in English and page 4 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: What I meant was that -- actually, this was a wrong interpretation of my words when I was providing the statement. The village of Kijani was not shelled. Shells never fell there. When I said that the village was hit, I meant that it was plundered and torched. That's what I meant by this word "hit."

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: What happened to your family's house?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: My mother and father had two houses, the old one and the new one, the latter having been constructed on the eve of Operation Storm. Both houses were looted and torched.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Can you show 65 ter 4853, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Mr. Sovilj, while we are waiting -- it's loading. Do you -- what is this photo?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: This photo depicts my parents' new house which looks just like you see it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: And who took this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: The photo was taken by my friends who went there and popped over either by chance or intentionally. They travelled through Kijani and they took this photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Can you go to page 2. And I believe there should be a translation available of what is written on page 2. I'm not sure if we can load the translation as well. In the meantime, Mr. Sovilj, can you read out what is written on this? Oh, it's not going to be necessary. What is this writing?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: This is on the back of the photo that we have just seen. It says here, "The house of Milena and Vlade Sovilj in the village of Kijani Gracac municipality destroyed in Storm in 1995."

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Thank you. And can these two pages of 62 ter be tendered into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P93, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P93 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just only have a couple more questions then I will be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes then if you would please finish before we adjourn for the day, that's four minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: How many people lived in Kijani before you left it in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: I can't be very precise. According to my estimate, between 70 and 80 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: And you mention in paragraph 13 of your statement you did not return to Croatia for safety reasons. Can you elaborate on that?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: I had never intended to go back to live there for several reasons. One of the reasons was also safety.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Where does your family live nowadays?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: In Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court who you have left of your family?

utterances.speaker: MILE SOVILJ
utterances.text: Unfortunately, my family has been halved. My father was killed during the war in his village and four years later, first my wife died, and then my mother due to the inability to adapt to a life as refugees and they just could not cope with everything that they had been through which means that only me and my son are now left.

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, that concludes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I inquire with the Defence counsel how much time they would need for cross-examination? Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will go first and I think I need let's say an hour and a half, two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course we'll not do that today. Other Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Mikulicic will cover all the topics and I don't anticipate any cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No questions at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Sovilj, we will conclude for the day and we will resume tomorrow. Just to prepare you already, you will find two judges tomorrow, I will not be there tomorrow but I will read carefully what your testimony is so don't be surprised if you find only two tomorrow. Mr. Sovilj, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, that is your testimony that you've given already today or you're still about to give tomorrow. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tomorrow, we'll start at 9.00 in Courtroom III. Mr. Usher, would you please escort Mr. Sovilj out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Frolich, what would we have missed if not only this witness would have told us that this was his parents house or the new house of his parents but if he would not have known who made that photograph, if he would not have known that the person who took that photograph apparently wrote at the photograph the same thing that is already testified. Similar questions I could put in relation to the tobacco box. The tobacco box once written with TA then with TO, is there any -- was there any dispute about this house being the destroyed house of the parents of this witness. Is there any dispute where apparently there has been some DNA analysis whether the reason why we final came to this person was through the tobacco box which then appears in a document read out in full, then we see a picture of this tobacco box? I fully understand how important that is for witnesses, but how important is it for us at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. This was merely meant to assist the Chamber in clarifying that the identification that were made in different documents related to the same body or the same individual. Therefore, there is, I believe, no dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no dispute about it. Why not then tell the Chamber, we have an autopsy report and Defence and Prosecution agree that it is an autopsy report related to the father of the witness and this has been confirmed by DNA. That's done in approximately 30 seconds whereas I think we spent altogether, and these are just two examples, and I insisted several, several, several times on efficiency in these matters. That is the Chamber would like to hear specifically where the parties apparently disagree and a bit to our surprise where there seems to be quite a lot of argument, we found yesterday that we had to ask for this information in addition to what the parties had presented. I again, I'm urging both parties really to try to use our court time as efficiently as possible and with full respect for the trial techniques you apparently are using in a very skilled way, nevertheless, please focus on the core issues. We will adjourn for the day. We'll adjourn until tomorrow, the 25th of April, 9.00 in the morning Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 25th day of April, 2008 at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.
